A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 28-page versions of the same TACO paper. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F can be matched reliably; no material comparison gaps remain.

before.justification: v2 reports original task-mapping experiments, TACO benchmark results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix generalization evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and the additional analyses and evaluations in Appendices C–F.

M1.justification: TACO’s embeddings, task guider, attention mechanism, losses, and inference procedure are retained. v4 identifies the existing Attention operator in Equation 11 as cross-attention and tidies notation, without establishing a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both retain the nine main benchmarks, GQA and A-OKVQA evaluations in Appendix E.5, and NLP Rule Learning and text-to-image Fast Counting evaluations in Appendix F.3. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within corresponding experiments: Table 1 retains RS, I2I, IQ2IQ, IQPR, DEmO, and Lever-LM. The Oracle variants and the appendix generalization and efficiency comparators are also retained.

E3.justification: Both retain the same five LVLMs, four-shot main evaluation, data splits, metrics, training budgets, and supplementary experimental settings. Table 4 reformats the existing instructions without changing their wording or use.

E4.justification: The task-mapping perturbations and cohesion probes, component ablations, shot-count studies, training-sequence comparisons, and appendix embedding, instruction, and failure-case analyses are unchanged. No analysis or associated evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix C.5 retains the repeated-experiment statement for Disruption Gap and ten random permutations for Order Sensitivity. Neither version adds different run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: All reported numerical entries, plotted findings, and qualitative outcomes are retained across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports TACO’s VQAv2 accuracy as 66.75 and HatefulMemes ROC-AUC as 80.59 in both versions under the same settings.

T1.justification: Appendix B’s formal definitions and the mathematical derivations are unchanged. Equation 9 replaces t_1^(l) with t_i^(l) in a branch explicitly restricted to i=1, making the expressions equivalent. Layer-symbol and superscript corrections standardize notation without changing mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the task-mapping framework, TACO’s sequence configuration approach, and claimed superiority across five LVLMs and nine main datasets. No core claim is strengthened, narrowed, or replaced.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning mapping cohesion, query importance, Oracle bias, and generalization remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning cognitive-science integration and investigation of task mapping’s internal realization.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly specifies that Attention(·,·) in Equation 11 denotes cross-attention, providing a limited implementation clarification. Existing hyperparameters, encoder training details, beam sizes, data construction instructions, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix A, and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. Changes in reference page boundaries reflect text reflow, not additions or removals.

P1.justification: v4 lightly edits Figure 1’s caption, standardizes attention-related notation, and adds one sentence explaining Equation 11’s operator. The section organization and broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 has adjusted column widths, spacing, and text wrapping. Figure 1’s caption reflows, and the Section 3 addition shifts subsequent text across page boundaries. No figures or tables are added or removed; plots and result-table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves technical clarity by explicitly identifying Equation 11’s cross-attention operation and making the associated notation consistent. These edits reduce ambiguity in the method description. The empirical evidence, theory, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to clarity and documentation.
